records.source_context: Robert Sanders, Manager of Science Communications at UC Berkeley, wrote, “Sunflowers not only pivot to face the sun as it moves across the sky during the day, but they also rotate 180 degrees during the night to greet the morning sun.” According to North Dakota State University’s Sunflower Production Guide, commercial sunflower growers typically grow one of three types of sunflower: oilseed types for vegetable oil, non-oilseed types for human food and bird food markets, and Conoil for dehull confection, oil, or bird food markets.

records.our_prose: The classic head-infesting pair. Sunflower moth (a small buff-gray moth) lays eggs as heads open; larvae tunnel into the seeds, web the face of the head, and can predispose it to Rhizopus head rot. The sunflower head-clipping weevil (metallic black, long snout) girdles the stalk 1 to 2 inches below the head, dropping it to the ground. Both are managed culturally in the garden: sanitation (destroy spent stalks and dropped heads), crop rotation away from continuous sunflower, and tolerance, since home-scale damage is usually limited.

records.our_prose: In California's desert valleys, sunflower is planted in late winter to early spring to bloom before and through the intense summer heat, which it tolerates well with deep watering; the season is essentially frost-bracketed only by brief, mild winter cold. Full sun, deep but infrequent watering to the taproot, and good drainage are key, with the heaviest water around bloom. Stake tall types against desert wind, and bag heads against birds for seed.

records.our_prose: In Florida, sunflowers grow best in the cooler, drier parts of the year. The University of Florida notes that seeds are planted in late winter to early spring, and the common sunflowers fade in the heat and humidity by late spring or early summer; a fall planting gives autumn flowers. Plant in full sun in warm soil, give plants room because humidity brings leaf diseases, water at the soil, and cover seed heads early to keep the many birds off.

records.our_prose: In the Florida peninsula, sunflower is grown mainly in the cooler, drier parts of the year: UF/IFAS notes seeds are sown in late winter to early spring, with the common annual sunflower declining in the heat and humidity by late spring to early summer, and a fall sowing giving an autumn show. Direct-sow into warm soil, site in full sun, and expect strong leaf-disease (rust, downy mildew, Septoria) and bird pressure in the humidity, so space generously, water at the base, and bag heads early to save seed.

records.our_prose: Keep moisture even as the head forms; the roughly 20 days before and after flowering are the critical water window, when shortage cuts head size and seed fill. Water deeply to the taproot, never to saturation.
records.source_context: Cultivars of giant sunflowers include: 'Cyclops' 'Mammoth Russian' 'American Giant' Maintenance Watering Sunflowers can withstand some drought. Water them regularly 20 days before and after flowering to encourage root growth, which is helpful with taller sunflower varieties bearing top-heavy blooms.

records.our_prose: Keep soil evenly moist through germination and establishment, then water deeply but less often; established sunflowers are notably drought-tolerant thanks to a deep taproot, but the roughly 20 days before and after flowering are the critical window when steady moisture builds the head and fills the seed.
